articles.title: Trump is headed to China this week. Jensen Huang won't be on the trip, but Elon Musk will.
articles.summary: President Trump is traveling to Asia for meetings on trade and other economic issues, but with the ongoing scandal at Nvidia hanging over the journey.
articles.body:
President Trump departed Monday for a trip to Asia that includes stops in the Philippines and China for meetings focused on trade and other economic issues, but with the ongoing scandal at Nvidia hanging over the journey.

"We're making a big trip ... mostly on economics but a lot of other things will be discussed," Trump told reporters as he previewed meetings with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin, even suggesting he might meet with North Korean leader Kim Jong Un.

Jensen Huang is not scheduled to join the trip, even as Trump continues to voice support for the former Nvidia ( NVDA ) CEO.

On Monday, Trump said he "would not mind" seeing Huang reinstated as some tech executives push for exactly that.

The White House has also confirmed that Tesla ( TSLA ) and SpaceX ( SPCX ) CEO Elon Musk will join at least during the China leg.

"He's a big part of our national security," a senior US official told reporters, adding that Musk will "be of tremendous benefit just even as an adviser to the president."

Musk is not the only business leader expected to cross paths with the president at a China-hosted CEO summit, one of the major stops of the week.

That gathering is being organized by a group called the China Council for the Promotion of International Trade, which announced Sunday that over 100 top global companies — including Apple ( AAPL ), Google ( GOOG ), Walmart ( WMT ), ExxonMobil ( XOM ), and Boeing ( BA ) — are set to be represented.

Mastercard ( MA ) CEO Michael Miebach will be another attendee, the South China Morning Post reported on Sunday, and Chinese state media added that 12 leaders of APEC economies will also attend.

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has signaled that his focus will be on establishing a new dialogue with China on AI to improve communication.

In a Fox News appearance on Sunday, Bessent raised new questions about what he called a "culture of noncompliance" at Nvidia that led to semiconductor exports potentially ending up in Chinese hands in recent years. He said Nvidia's board of directors should go outside the company for a new executive as part of a "dramatic shake-up."

The summit of business leaders occurs just ahead of an Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) gathering being held Nov. 18-19 in Shenzhen, China

Trump's first stop is a gathering of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) in the Philippines that opened over the weekend . The president is set to land in Manila on Tuesday evening, local time.

Trump is expected to sign a trade deal with Thailand as part of those meetings alongside what the White House is previewing as other "commercial deals," one of which is expected to focus on aviation.

articles.title: Rural voters revolted because they wanted Republicans to help them. GOP didn’t deliver
articles.summary: Diesel at $5.25 a gallon, timber production down 79% and soaring farm costs fueled a rural voter revolt that cost Republicans key Senate seats.
articles.body: Rural counties swung more than 15 percentage points toward Democrats in the 2026 midterms. Republicans lost rural strongholds including Iowa, South Carolina and Kansas, where a Democrat won a U.S. Senate seat for the first time since 1932. Republicans haven’t fully lost rural America, but they got one heck of a warning. Just before the election, a national survey of rural voters found that about 75% rated their local cost of living as fair or poor. Nearly half worried about making their rent or mortgage payments. FOX NEWS POLL: SQUEEZED BY COSTS, FRUSTRATED VOTERS TURN TO THE DEMOCRATS The GOP doesn't need another consultant's postmortem to understand what happened. It needs to look at what's happening to the people who feed, build and power this country. Farm production expenses are projected to reach nearly $493 billion in 2026, up 4.5% in a single year, while inflation-adjusted net farm income is expected to fall 5.5%. In 2012, John Deere's flagship combine cost roughly $454,000, when wheat was $7.77 a bushel. Today, its flagship combine costs over $1.1 million, while wheat is projected at $6.91 a bushel. Meanwhile, family farm bankruptcies jumped 46% in 2025. BROOKE ROLLINS, MONICA CROWLEY: AMERICA’S FAMILY FARMS HAVE KEPT US STRONG FOR 250 YEARS Ranchers are seeing record cattle prices, but production costs have climbed nearly 30% since 2020. Ranchers also face a government-enabled meatpacking oligopoly where four companies account for roughly 85% of steer and heifer purchases. Federal regulations make opening independent processing facilities prohibitively expensive, leaving ranchers with fewer buyers and little negotiating power. CUT THE BULL: THE REAL REASON BEEF COSTS SO MUCH — AND WHAT TRUMP IS TRYING TO DO Washington's response to agricultural hardship increasingly involves writing checks. Direct government farm payments are projected to reach $47.4 billion this year. Assistance can keep operations alive, but subsidies don't make equipment cheaper or create new markets. Too often, that money flows straight through farmers to banks, lenders, equipment manufacturers and chemical suppliers. Farmers become little more than conduits for taxpayer dollars, collecting a government check with one hand and handing it over to the industries squeezing them with the other. Counterintuitively, tariffs have increased costs for imported machinery, steel and agricultural inputs while exposing American exports to retaliation. Farmers are expected to compete globally while the tools of competition get more expensive. AMERICAN BUSINESSES AREN’T ALLOWED TO BUILD. IT’S TIME CONGRESS HELPED THEM The timber industry has fared just as poorly. In 1988, America's national forests produced 12.6 billion board feet of timber. By 2024, that figure had collapsed to just 2.7 billion, a 79% decline. Federal regulations, bureaucratic roadblocks and relentless litigation have strangled timber production, shuttered sawmills and devastated communities that depended on these jobs for generations. Adding insult to injury, federal law can even force taxpayers to foot the legal bills for environmental groups that successfully sue to block timber projects. Meanwhile, millions of acres have gone up in flames across America this year, while the sawmills that once turned those trees into lumber sit shuttered in towns now choking on wildfire smoke from timber that used to build American homes. Republicans promised to take a chainsaw to federal bureaucracy. Instead, chainsaws are sitting idle as timber mills rust into the ground. The Trump administration deserves credit for proposing to repeal Clinton’s 2001 Roadless Rule. But the repeal remains unfinished and would only scratch the surface of what is needed to reignite our timber industry. Ranchers are seeing record cattle prices, but production costs have climbed nearly 30% since 2020. Along with timber, America needs domestic copper, silver and critical minerals to power its future and create high-paying jobs. Yet it takes nearly 29 years to open a new mine, longer than anywhere in the world except Zambia. Coal production is projected to fall 2% in 2026. Even with record American oil production, diesel is expected to average $5.25 a gallon. Coal towns face declining production while farmers and truckers pay a fortune for fuel. A Republican trifecta was supposed to deliver American energy dominance. But while D.C. loves the products of rural industry, it stands in the way of the industries themselves. AMERICA'S TRUCKERS ISSUE DIRE WARNING AS SOARING DIESEL COSTS THREATEN 'DOMINO EFFECT' Take all this bureaucracy, overregulation and financial hardship together, and it’s no wonder Republicans heard a harsh rebuke from rural America on Election Day. In 2024, voters who described themselves as financially struggling favored President Donald Trump by roughly 30 points. In 2026, voters describing the same circumstances favored Democrats by approximately 30 points. MEHEK COOKE: REPUBLICANS FAILED THE AFFORDABILITY TEST. THIS IS HOW TO WIN VOTERS BACK Republicans have made real progress on tax reform, preventing one of the largest tax increases in American history and proposing meaningful regulatory reforms. But preventing a tax increase doesn't make diesel or fertilizer cheaper. Proposing regulatory reform isn't the same as delivering it. And families struggling to make ends meet aren't interested in hearing how much worse things could have been. Republicans shouldn't mistake the midterms for rural America suddenly embracing socialist economic policies. The warning is simpler: people are frustrated with the cost of living, disappearing opportunities and a political system better at managing their problems than solving them. The answer isn’t more government, it's freedom. Republicans need to start acting like the party that believes in it. Keep fighting for tax cuts, American innovation and fiscal responsibility. Those battles matter. But it's time to listen to congressional Republicans who actually represent rural America and understand what’s needed to revive the communities that put the GOP in power cycle after cycle. Coal production is projected to fall 2% in 2026. Even with record American oil production, diesel is expected to average $5.25 a gallon. Start by passing the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act, now before the Senate, to reform the Endangered Species Act and overhaul federal permitting. Reform the Equal Access to Justice Act so taxpayers aren't footing the legal bills for groups that sue to block logging, mining and energy development. Reform the Federal Meat Inspection Act to eliminate unnecessary barriers to independent meat processing and give ranchers more buyers and greater freedom to compete. CLICK HERE FOR MORE FOX NEWS OPINION Put these reforms on the floor. Force votes. If Democrats kill them, put them on record, make them defend it. Republicans cannot distinguish themselves from Democrats with another federal program, subsidy or tariff. Rural Americans don't want a handout or another promise. They want leaders who will fight for their freedom to do the work that built this country. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP The GOP lost the House and the Senate. If they lose rural America, they won’t regain power for a generation.

articles.title: AI bubble will likely burst and cause a recession by 2028 election, Wall Street’s former top cop says
articles.summary: The artificial intelligence boom is a bubble that will likely burst and cause a recession prior to the 2028 presidential election, Gary Gensler, the former top cop on Wall Street, told CNN.
articles.body: The artificial intelligence boom is a bubble that will likely burst and cause a recession prior to the 2028 presidential election, Gary Gensler, the former top cop on Wall Street, told CNN. “It’s already a bubble,” Gensler, who was the point person overseeing US capital markets during the Biden administration, said in an interview. Gensler’s warning comes at a precarious moment for the AI industry following a cascading series of shocks in recent weeks. Democrats’ stunning midterm victories raised fears among investors of a looming crackdown on the data centers at the heart of the AI buildout. Washington and Wall Street are still feeling the shockwaves caused by the stunning downfall of Nvidia’s Jensen Huang, the most important person in the industry. And now a critical test looms: Anthropic is attempting to pull off a record-shattering IPO in the face of these headwinds. Gensler, who led the Securities and Exchange Commission from 2021 until 2025, pointed to the mind-boggling amounts of money – by some estimates $800 billion a year – being plowed into building AI infrastructure. “History tells us that when you have a new technology and a significant investment…you come to a point where it plateaus. It retrenches,” said Gensler. “The only question is if it’s a soft recession or something more dramatic.” The comments appear to make Gensler the most senior former federal regulator to publicly warn that an AI-fueled recession may be on the way. But his words of caution echo similar AI bubble-bursting warnings from prominent individuals on Wall Street and academics, including hedge fund billionaire Ray Dalio, Harvard economist Kenneth Rogoff and investor Mike Novogratz. Gold rush meets arms race Gensler, now a professor at MIT, pointed to past examples of transformative technologies over centuries that experienced powerful downturns after infrastructure was funded in anticipation of revenue. “That railroad boom-to-bubble was quite an adventure, and it led to really deep recessions, depressions. The 1920s with electricity, the 1990s with the internet,” Gensler said. With AI, companies have scrambled to sink enormous sums of money into building data centers, buying cutting-edge computer chips and other equipment. There is a race to build the smartest models and the best chips to cash in on an epic gold rush on Wall Street and to beat China in a high-stakes arms race for tech superiority. But money is pouring in to this space faster than the ability to turn a profit – an unsustainable mismatch that must eventually come into balance, one way or another. ‘Too much money, too fast’ All of this raises the specter of companies overinvesting and piling on too much debt. “The Big Tech companies are spending five times more in 2026 than they were just three years ago…It’s just the extraordinary size of it all,” Gensler said. Nvidia’s financial tentacles reach almost every corner of the AI ecosystem, to the point that the company has been dubbed the central bank of AI, with Huang its chairman – until his sudden exit last week. It’s not just the spending that worries AI skeptics. It’s how this binge is being funded. Gensler, who served as chairman of the Commodity Futures Trading Commission during the Obama administration, expressed concern that some of this spending has been hidden from view. He pointed to circular financing and complex, off-balance sheet financing that make it difficult to understand just how much risk is being taken on. “One might question why all the lenders are lending all this money,” Gensler said. “I think history will show that they loaned too much money, too fast. And that’s the nature of these types of booms that become bursted bubbles.” ‘Breakage and bankruptcies’ So if this boom goes bust, where will the first dominos fall? Gensler pointed to neoclouds, the specialized cloud-based platforms that lease out massive amounts of specialized supercomputing brainpower to AI developers. The problem is that some of these companies have built their businesses on a mountain of debt and their business models are vulnerable to sudden shifts. “The major companies will survive. It’s these neocloud companies where we’re going to see some breakage and bankruptcies,” Gensler said. Elon Musk ominously warned that the 200-plus existing neoclouds will experience “guppy-level death and consolidation.” “Some will make it through, but not many,” Musk said in a post on X last month. Boom-to-bust cycles in housing, dot-com Of course, not all bursted bubbles cause recessions – and not all of them are severe. Gensler said he expects the magnitude of this potential downturn to be “as significant as” the dot-com bubble bursting in the early 2000s but not “as harsh as” the subprime mortgage meltdown that led to the 2008 financial crisis. And just as the Great Recession served as a powerful backdrop to the 2008 race for the White House, Gensler said this potential downturn could arrive at a critical time in the political calendar. “I think we’re going to have this repricing and a softening of the economy that happens before November 2028,” he said. ‘No irrational exuberance’ Of course, many on Wall Street believe the past few weeks prove how durable the AI boom really is. AI stocks have lost significant altitude but they have not imploded and investors have not panicked – despite the recent shocks. “What we’re seeing here is the air coming out of the bubble. It doesn’t have to burst,” said Ed Yardeni, president of Yardeni Research. “I don’t see this as a bubble that bursts. It’s a self-correcting bubble. Every now and then you get a swoon in the AI trade.” Yardeni, who was the top economist at Deutsche Bank during the bursting of the dot-com bubble, conceded that Gensler’s warning is a “plausible scenario” but added that bubble fears are preventing an unsustainable melt-up. “If everyone is convinced that AI is a bubble, it probably isn’t. It’s good that people like Gensler are keeping us all grounded because in some ways that reduces the downside,” Yardeni said. Some of these concerns have helped deflate once-lofty valuation metrics, lowering the risk that stocks become untethered to reality. Yardeni pointed to how price-to-earnings ratios for chipmakers have tumbled below that of the broader market. “We’re not looking at 1999-2000 all over again. There is no irrational exuberance in valuations,” he said. Storm on the horizon? The former SEC chairman said he believes in the “underlying technology” powering AI but still worries capital markets are mispricing it. Gensler, who grew up on the Chesapeake Bay, likened the current moment to sailing with ominous clouds on the horizon. “I can’t say exactly when and how stormy,” he said, “but I would be battening down some hatches and making sure you have some proper rain gear.”

articles.title: A growing share of homeowners don't have a mortgage at all
articles.summary: More than 40% of homeowners don't have a mortgage at all, giving them more flexibility in the high-rate era.
articles.body:
Mortgage rates above 7% have put the housing market in a deep slump and left millions of prospective homebuyers struggling to figure out how they'll be able to afford to buy.

But there's a growing share of homeowners who can look past the rate noise, because they don't have any mortgage at all. The share of owner-occupied homes owned outright jumped to 41% last year, according to a Realtor.com analysis of Census Bureau data. The number has been rising steadily over the years, from about 33% in 2010.

Homeowners who own outright have more flexibility than those who still have mortgages. Free-and-clear owners who want to move often have enough equity to pay for their next home in cash, insulating them from the effects of mortgage rate shocks. And unlike many of their peers with low-rate mortgages, they don't feel tied down to a home that might no longer meet their needs.

Many of the markets with the lowest share of mortgaged homes are relatively affordable areas like Buffalo, N.Y., Pittsburgh, and Oklahoma City. But it's the retirement hotspot of Miami that has the largest share of homes owned outright at nearly 46%.

Claire Boston is a senior reporter for Yahoo Finance covering housing, mortgages, and home insurance.

articles.title: Blackstone REIT to Buy Amazon Data Centers in $5 Billion Deal
articles.summary: Blackstone Inc.’s newly listed data center acquisition vehicle has acquired a majority interest in two joint ventures with Amazon Web Services in a transacti...
articles.body:
(Bloomberg) -- Blackstone Inc.'s newly listed data center acquisition vehicle has acquired a majority interest in two joint ventures with Amazon Web Services in a transaction valued at roughly $5 billion.

In its first-ever investment, Blackstone Digital Infrastructure Trust Inc. will own 13 newly constructed powered shells across two AWS data center campuses in northern Indiana and Mississippi, according to Nick Pell, chief executive of the fund known as BXDC.

BXDC will acquire a majority interest of 75% and AWS will retain 25%, and the hyperscaler will lease back the whole portfolio with an initial term of 12 years extendable to 32 years, according to a statement Monday.

"This direct deal with Amazon creates a roadmap to do more such deals with hyperscalers or developers," Pell said in an interview. The joint venture has a debt commitment to borrow 50% of the purchase price at close, according to Pell. The transaction is expected to be completed this year.

The real estate investment trust encapsulates Blackstone's ambition to become one of the largest backers of artificial intelligence infrastructure and its push to reach more individual investors. The nearly $1.4 trillion alternative asset manager has amassed a $200 billion data center portfolio that includes QTS Realty Trust, a leading builder and operator of such facilities.

Listed in May, BXDC has set out to acquire stabilized data centers valued between $250 million and $1.5 billion and with long-term lease contracts with hyperscalers, an addressable market the fund estimates at $1 trillion over the next five years.

"There are a lot of developers and close-ended funds looking to exit and recycle their capital and we are finding a home for them with the public investor capital in BXDC," Pell said.

The Democratic sweep in midterm elections is set to give momentum to the party's drive to set guard rails on the growth of data centers. Development of the facilities has come up against organized opposition from communities as well as supply shortages for equipment, creating bottlenecks.

More than 60% of the data center capacity planned for completion in 2027 has yet to begin construction, according to a May report from JPMorgan Chase & Co.

articles.title: Billionaire Ron Baron Says SpaceX Will Be Worth $30 Trillion by 2040. At $141 a Share, Here’s the Annual Return That Requires.
articles.summary: Hitting this market cap milestone will be no small feat, given how the space and AI company is starting off in the trillion-dollar club.
articles.body:
It's safe to say fund manager Ron Baron is a big fan of Space Exploration Technologies (NASDAQ:SPCX), better known as SpaceX. The billionaire investor first invested in SpaceX nearly ten years ago. Even after its trillion-dollar initial public offering (IPO), Baron remains bullish.

In fact, back in May, when interviewed by CNBC about the IPO, he stated that SpaceX could "become the largest company on the planet," becoming worth as much as $30 trillion over the next "ten to fifteen years." Baron further backed his statement by buying an additional $1 billion in SpaceX shares. Yet while Baron may be extremely confident in SpaceX's long-term potential, achieving this goal will require exceptional growth.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

SpaceX currently trades for around $141 per share, giving it a market cap of around $1.92 trillion. That means a move to a $30 trillion market cap means around a 1,460% gain. If SpaceX were to make this move in 10 years, this would equate to a 31.6% annualized return. If it hit it in 14 years, this would equate to a 21.7% annualized return.

Of course, these calculations are based on the assumption that there's no major share dilution during this time frame. If recent reports prove true, and SpaceX and Tesla merger talks are moving along, the combination of these two Elon Musk investments would result in a company with a market cap exceeding $3 trillion. This would result in a much lower annualized return hurdle to hit the $30 trillion mark.

Achieving 20% to 30% annualized returns for a decade or more is no small feat. Some megacap stocks have achieved it in the past, but none of them began these impressive runs from a trillion-dollar starting point.

Baron believes Musk's space exploration and AI innovations "could make the economy grow 10 times in 10 years, not double." Still, given Musk's tendency to overpromise and underdeliver, it may be best to wait for SpaceX to further execute on its Starlink, Starship, and X.ai growth efforts before entering a long-term position.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 14x Bigger

Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005.

But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout, a massive technology build-out that Google's CEO says could be more profound than fire or electricity.

articles.title: Buy Nvidia stock or wait? A guide to making the call on any stock.
articles.summary: Nvidia's CEO Jensen Huang resigned, pushing NVDA stock to a multiyear low. Use this 7-question guide to decide whether the dip is a buying opportunity.
articles.body:
Some offers on this page are from advertisers who pay us, which may affect which products we write about, but not our recommendations. See our Advertiser Disclosure .

Nvidia ( NVDA ), one of the world's most valuable companies, lost nearly 30% of its value between mid-October and mid-November. The catalysts? The slide began with concerns about the sustainability of AI infrastructure spending and continued after a scandal pushed co-founder and CEO Jensen Huang to resign.

NVDA's dramatic price dip is either a discount-buying opportunity or a red flag to steer clear. What's important is choosing your interpretation from the lens of a consistent, repeatable investing process. Aligning your decision on Nvidia with the rest of your portfolio helps you manage risk and maintain assets you can hold for the long term.

In the 12 months before July 26, 2026, Nvidia produced more than $300 billion in revenue and $192 billion in net income. The semiconductor company is the dominant supplier of AI-capable processing chips. Strong demand from data centers and hyperscalers over the last three years has propelled Nvidia to a market capitalization of $3.9 trillion, second only to Apple ( AAPL ).

Qualities to like about Nvidia include the company's strong revenue growth, high margins, and dominant market position in a fast-growing space. Former CEO Jensen Huang was also considered by many to be a savvy and effective leader.

How to decide whether to buy a stock: 7 questions to guide your decision

Nvidia's price drop generally shouldn't, in itself, push you to invest in the stock — particularly if it will be your first equity purchase outside of a 401(k). Investing decisions are best approached with discipline because there is real risk involved. If you're new to the game, use these seven questions as your guide.

Should you be buying individual stocks at all?

Individual stocks can gain and lose value quickly. Case in point: Nvidia lost nearly 30% in the past month. If you had $50,000 in Nvidia alone, your account value would have declined by almost $15,000 in a few short weeks.

Many investors manage that volatility by diversifying, which involves owning companies that operate in different industries and sometimes in different countries and currencies. Experts commonly recommend holding at least 20 individual and noncompeting companies.

A portfolio with 20 individual stocks requires ongoing maintenance. If you don't have the time or interest in monitoring and managing your stocks, you may prefer an index-fund portfolio instead. Broad market index funds are already diversified, so you may only need one or two.

Do you understand how the company makes money?

When you understand how a company makes money, you can better evaluate news, developments, and earnings reports.

Nvidia makes money selling semiconductors. While data center and hyperscaler demand generates the most revenue, the company also sells to the automotive, gaming, and robotics markets. Demand for AI chips is strong as companies invest in their AI capabilities for the first time. There's also a refresh cycle for semiconductors that sets up the potential for ongoing demand when the initial AI build-out winds down. Nvidia's customers want the most powerful chips, and Nvidia delivers by continually improving product performance.

Quality businesses sell products or services that are essential or deliver real value. They have a solid competitive advantage that discourages other companies from replicating what they do. They generate growing revenues and cash flow. And they have opportunities to invest their excess cash profitably.

One of Nvidia's recognized competitive advantages is its software ecosystem. Customers develop on the company's CUDA platform, which runs on Nvidia hardware. Switching to competing hardware could require rewriting and re-optimizing code. Nvidia also has a strong revenue and cash flow record, and has successfully grown the business through strong R&D and computing investments.

Evaluating a stock's price can be complicated. Many investors simplify the process by analyzing valuation metrics, including ratios like price-to-earnings (PE) and price-to-sales (PS). The PE and PS ratios are best used for comparing the company's stock price to competitors and to the company's own history.

Price/earnings-to-growth, known as the PEG ratio, is another valuation metric to know. The PEG ratio incorporates the company's expected growth rate, so the resulting value is more widely comparable. A PEG ratio near 1 is considered fairly valued. Lower PEG ratios are associated with undervalued stocks, and a PEG above 2 implies a premium on the expected growth.

Nvidia's PE ratio, as of Nov. 13, is in the low 20s, well below the company's five-year average. It's also low compared to other semiconductor stocks, including Taiwan Semiconductor ( TSM ), Broadcom ( AVGO ), and Credo Technology ( CRDO ). NVDA's PEG ratio of 0.2 is solidly in the undervalued category.

High PE and PS ratios can result when investors expect a company to produce strong growth. If the expected growth doesn't materialize, volatility can result. For that reason, it's important to know what's driving a company's valuation ratios. Only then can you decide if the risk is worth it.

In Nvidia's case, investors are pricing in negative factors. The primary concern is the loss of the company's CEO, on top of lingering uncertainty about how long the AI infrastructure spending spree will last.

What could break the thesis? How much, and how?

Your investment thesis is the case for owning a stock: why you expect it to grow in value and what has to stay true for that to happen. Analyze what factors could prevent the company from meeting these expectations. This is where understanding the business model can be invaluable. You can review earnings transcripts, analyst coverage, and industry research to identify potential risks.

The surprise resignation of Nvidia's CEO is a thesis-breaking factor. Those who bought Nvidia when it was 30% higher likely didn't predict this scenario. Many investors prefer to manage these risks by buying stocks at prices well below their estimated intrinsic value. This strategy creates a margin of safety against unknowns.

When you consider buying a stock, it's also wise to consider selling it. Identifying the factors that would prompt you to sell helps you make better decisions as circumstances change. If slow sales growth, loss of a key customer, or departure of the CEO are your exit triggers, then you know what to do if those situations arise. Document your triggers in detail so you don't second-guess yourself later.

Exit triggers for Nvidia in the post-Huang era might include strategy changes, missed or delayed product launches, or declining margins.

Should you buy a stock before or after earnings?

Nvidia reports third-quarter earnings on Nov. 17. The decision to buy before that date hinges on your risk tolerance. Buying early could be profitable if the earnings report or the company's outlook is better than expected. But that decision comes with the risk of another pullback if the results or guidance are disappointing.

Postponing your investment decision until after the earnings release gives you more information to evaluate. In this case, Nvidia's new leadership team may present information that could sway your opinion on the stock.

Buying the dip vs. catching a falling knife

A temporary dip in stock price is an opportunity. A lingering stock-price decline is a trap. These questions can help you differentiate one from the other.

Questions to ask before buying a pullback

Has the thesis changed or just the price? Exercise caution if the business has fundamentally changed for the worse.

What are analysts and insiders saying? Be wary if analysts are cutting their price targets, insiders are selling, or the company's guidance is softening.

Can the company absorb the problem financially? Companies with liquidity and cash flow can often survive temporary disruptions.

Does the company still have its competitive advantage? A weakening competitive advantage is a red flag.

Does it fit your investing parameters? A stock that's on sale isn't automatically a good fit. Take the time to evaluate the business and decide if the stock would help or hurt your portfolio.

Common mistakes when deciding when to buy a stock

You can have a thorough investing process and still make mistakes. Some of the common ones to watch for are as follows:

Buying trendy stocks: Trendy stocks are expensive and, often, volatile. If the stock doesn't truly fit your investing style, you're more likely to sell when things get tough.

Making quick decisions: Without disciplined decision-making, you're gambling, not investing.

Over-investing in one stock or industry: A concentrated portfolio is more likely to be volatile.

Trying to time the market for quick gains: Timing the market successfully requires being right when you buy and again when you sell. It's hard to do once, let alone consistently enough to outpace a buy-and-hold approach.

Nvidia has hit a multiyear low, but the company's future is more uncertain without Huang at the helm. If you believe the rest of Nvidia's leadership team can step in and fulfill the former co-founder's vision, this downturn could be a buying opportunity. If not, wait for Nvidia's next earnings release to learn more.

Buying Nvidia before earnings could be a consideration if you believe the company will report better-than-expected results and a solid outlook.

Nvidia has been a high-performing stock. The company has high margins, a healthy balance sheet, and an enviable market position. But with the recent resignation of co-founder and CEO Jensen Huang, the company's trajectory may change.

Several analysts either downgraded their recommendation on Nvidia or lowered their price target after Huang announced his resignation. The average price target is still more than 75% higher than the trading price.

You can test a stock's price for value by comparing its margins, metrics, and financial results to competitors. Metrics like the price-to-earnings and price-to-sales ratios quantify the stock price relative to earnings and sales. Comparing these values to competitors and to the company's own history can signal whether the stock price is compelling.

It is better to buy a stock when it's down if the price decline is temporary. Temporary price dips can result when the market overreacts to economic trends, industry headlines, or company developments.

Many investors cap single stocks at about 5% of their portfolio.

articles.title: Nvidia can replace Jensen Huang, but not the handshakes behind its chips: Chart of the Day
articles.summary: Nvidia's suppliers run on deals that Jensen Huang never put in writing.
articles.body:
A Jensen Huang comeback is a 1-in-9 long shot on prediction markets, and Dan Ives calls it "ridiculous." Nvidia's ( NVDA ) supply chain, built on his handshakes, makes it less ridiculous than it sounds.

Days after Huang resigned as Nvidia CEO amid affair scandals, the Financial Times reported Sunday that he has discussed a return, and allies are building a Silicon Valley "war room" to lobby the board.

Nvidia stock is on track for its lowest close since early July 2025, about a third below its October record. The company's first earnings report without Huang comes Tuesday after the market close.

Yorkville's Ives said "no one individual can replace Jensen as CEO," but he called a comeback "ridiculous in our view given the legal/Board/DC scrutiny/moral compass/China tentacles."

The case for Huang starts with paperwork that doesn't exist. He has said Nvidia has never signed a contract with chipmaker TSMC ( TSM ) in three decades of business. Elon Musk, who backs a petition to bring Huang back, wrote on X that many deals "were a handshake with Jensen, not a written contract" and that "without Jensen, at least some of those critical deals will be lost."

The scale is staggering. One Vera Rubin rack, Nvidia's newest AI system, holds 1.3 million parts, per the company's count, from a supply chain twice the size of the one behind Blackwell. More than 150 partners in Taiwan alone help build it.

Nvidia had lined up $279 billion in supply and capacity commitments as of July, according to its latest quarterly filing . That's 17 times the total in January 2024. About $267 billion comes due in the next 2.5 years, and some of those deals can be canceled or adjusted before firm orders are placed.

Bettors took notice. Polymarket odds that Huang takes any formal role at Nvidia by year-end nearly doubled to about 20% after the FT report, then drifted down to about 11% Monday morning.

Nvidia's own annual report warns it is "highly dependent on the services of our longstanding executive team." And Huang ran the company with about 60 direct reports.

"How can you have the world's most valuable company and no kind of succession plan, not even anyone being groomed, [and] 60 people reporting to Jensen?" former Medtronic chair and CEO Bill George told Yahoo Finance .

The board isn't rolling out the welcome mat for Huang. It has approached Arm ( ARM ) CEO Rene Haas about the job, the FT reported, and Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent wants a dramatic shake-up with an outside CEO.

Not everyone buys the indispensable-founder pitch. "I'm not Jensen … but I know how little of the actual work that I do," Cisco chair and CEO Chuck Robbins told Yahoo Finance, pointing to Nvidia's "42,000 employees that wake up every day and go to the office and do a great job."

A dedicated GCC pavilion at the summit will showcase the ecosystem and encourage companies to undertake more intellectual property creation and high-value work from Karnataka.Kharge highlighted the state’s strengths in aerospace, electronics manufacturing and bioeconomy. Around 65% of aerospace manufacturing happens in Karnataka, which also accounts for about 21% of the country’s bioeconomy.Govt is seeking to distribute economic activity across the state through its Beyond Bengaluru policy, encouraging GCCs to establish operations in cities such as Mangaluru. Its Local Economic Acceleration Programme aims to develop regional clusters, with Kalaburagi being positioned as a bioeconomy hub, leveraging its potential in turmeric and pulses.These priorities will feature at the 29th edition of Bengaluru Tech Summit, themed ‘AI and Beyond’. More than 65 countries are expected to participate, with over 10,000 delegates, 700 speakers and 1,500 exhibitors. articles.title: Fed’s Schmid says central bank has ‘work to do’ on inflation
articles.summary: Jeffrey Schmid, the president of the Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City, said Sunday central bank officials have “work to do” to rein in persistent inflation. “As Chairman Kevin Warsh said at the Kansas City Fed’s Jackson Hole Economic Symposium in August, the Fed has some work to do on inflation, and, unfortunately, our work…
articles.body:
Jeffrey Schmid, the president of the Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City, said Sunday central bank officials have “work to do” to rein in persistent inflation .

“As Chairman Kevin Warsh said at the Kansas City Fed’s Jackson Hole Economic Symposium in August, the Fed has some work to do on inflation, and, unfortunately, our work has only gotten harder since then,” Schmid said at a National Credit Union Management Association conference in Hawaii .

“Inflation has been running too hot,” he added.

Schmid said that annual inflation, which rose to 3.6 percent in September according to the personal consumption expenditures price index, was “uncomfortably above” the Federal Reserve’s 2 percent target.

Another inflation metric, the consumer price index (CPI), measured prices as up 3.7 percent year over year in September.

The CPI increased by 0.4 percent from September to October , but the Bureau of Labor Statistics was unable to collect enough data in October 2025 — as a result of the record-long government shutdown that took up the entirety of that month — to provide annual inflation data.

Schmid cited four reasons for persistently elevated inflation: energy price shocks amid the Iran war , increases in durable goods prices, the artificial intelligence build-out and mounting healthcare costs for employers and ObamaCare enrollees .

The Kansas City Fed president said the central bank has the tools to address these price pressures, noting inflation “is always the result of an imbalance” between supply and demand.

“It is in the context of strong demand that a disruption to supply drives up prices. Demand always plays a role in inflation, and the Fed, through its influence on demand, always has the tools and responsibility to address inflation,” Schmid added.

Schmid does not sit on the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC), which will meet Dec. 8-9. The panel hiked interest rates by a quarter point in September, as officials seek to bring inflation down to 2 percent.

At last month’s FOMC meeting, officials held rates steady at a range of 3.75 percent to 4 percent. Traders are pricing in a 92.4 percent chance of officials raising rates in early December by a quarter point, and a 7.6 percent chance of a half-point hike, according to the CME FedWatch tool .

articles.title: SpaceX's Starship feat should remind investors that the company at its 'core' is a rocket builder
articles.summary: It was an absolutely massive day for  SpaceX and the rocket industry.
articles.body:
It was a massive day for SpaceX ( SPCX ) — and the rocket industry.

On Saturday, the company "caught" the upper stage, or Starship, of its largest rocket for the first time. The mission — Starship 15 — took off on Friday night, with Starship deploying 26 Starlink V3 satellites and orbiting Earth several times before returning to Starbase, Texas, where it was caught by the Mechazilla platform.

It wasn't a perfect launch, as the lower-stage Super Heavy booster experienced an issue and had to abort its catch. CEO Elon Musk said the Super Heavy booster was slightly low on fuel, hence the abort, but that anomaly is essentially a "footnote in an otherwise historic mission," William Blair analyst Louie DiPalma wrote on Monday morning.

DiPalma added, "In our view, this Starship catch will take the throne for the most famous catch in history from Willie Mays 1954 World Series catch in Major League Baseball's fall classic."

Evercore ISI analyst Kutgun Maral wrote that the Starship 15 launch should remind investors that SpaceX is, at its "core," a rocket builder, and that should underpin much of its value.

"While the never-ending SpaceX newsflow and its stock implications keep us busy day to day, the long-term value of this company will be decided less by the next GW of compute or the next contract renewal than by the cost and frequency of access to orbit," Maral wrote in a note to investors. "That is why Starship has been at the center of our thesis since our initiation — it underpins aspirations for broadband, mobile, orbital compute and, ultimately, the mission itself."

But it was also a "tale of two cities" for the space sector this weekend, as Blair's DiPalma said, flagging United Launch Alliance's setback with its Vulcan rocket on Sunday, with an "anomaly" leading to a lost rocket.

The Vulcan rocket, ULA's newest, lost all 40 Amazon Leo (Project Kuiper) broadband internet satellites on board. ULA is a joint venture between Boeing ( BA ) and Lockheed Martin ( LMT ).

"We will work closely with our customer and other appropriate organizations to find the cause, determine the appropriate corrective action, and return to flight as quickly as possible," ULA said in a statement .

"ULA's struggles have taken place during an era in which SpaceX has perfected reusable launch. Over the past 3 years, the Vulcan system has completed 4 successful missions compared with nearly 500 for SpaceX," DiPalma wrote.

Prior to this weekend's mishap, ULA achieved more than 150 consecutive successful launches before experiencing its first total mission failure on Sunday.

articles.title: Trump acknowledges 'different views' among aides as his administration advances new limits on semiconductor exports
articles.summary: The Trump administration announced on Monday that it is moving to close a perceived loophole in US export controls for advanced semiconductors.
articles.body:
The Trump administration announced on Monday that it is moving to close a perceived loophole in US export controls for advanced semiconductors as bipartisan questions about the role of Nvidia ( NVDA ) in possible national security lapses intensify.

The raging debate has split the Trump administration over how the US government should respond to the scandal at the chipmaker, with President Trump acknowledging that there are "two different views" among his aides.

Trump said some are leery of insulting China with harsh new restrictions, while others want to crack down. The president said he will make the final decision about how his government approaches the issue.

"I don't think you want to insult China just before you get there," Trump added before he departed for a trip to Asia that includes a China stop . "We're having a very good relationship with China right now." He did not address the new export rules directly.

T he Commerce Department's Bureau of Industry and Security, which oversees export control measures, advanced a rule to limit China's ability to access advanced chips that reside in data centers outside its borders.

The "interim final rule," the release noted, was "written by and at the direction of the Department of Treasury and the National Security Council" and moves the restrictions one step closer to being enacted.

The rules would limit access to sensitive American technology by cracking down on remote computing arrangements that allow Chinese companies to rent computing power in third countries.

It is a move to close what many see as a loophole that has allowed China to sidestep bans and access advanced chips provided by companies like Nvidia.

The announcement from Secretary Howard Lutnick's Commerce Department came as Lutnick faces bipartisan questions on whether he has slow-walked efforts in recent years to limit chip exports and even drawn criticism from other members of the Trump Cabinet.

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has notably declined to defend Lutnick's actions in a series of recent television appearances. On Fox News on Sunday , Bessent also discussed what he termed a "culture of noncompliance" at Nvidia, which he said led to semiconductor exports potentially ending up in Chinese hands.

Bessent said Nvidia needs "a dramatic shake-up" and should "go outside the company" ‌ as it seeks a new chief executive.

That last point is the subject of dispute among Trump's advisers, with Bessent staking out a sharply critical position while Elon Musk leads a petition to reinstate Huang .

articles.title: Eli Lilly is trouncing Nvidia — and the weight-loss drug trade is beating AI again
articles.summary: Since its Oct. 6 record, Nvidia has shed more than $1.7 trillion in market value. Eli Lilly has added more than $250 billion over the same stretch, a gain to...
articles.body:
Wall Street put the AI trade on a diet six weeks ago. The maker of Zepbound has been doing the bulking up.

Since its Oct. 6 record, Nvidia ( NVDA ) has shed more than $1.7 trillion in market value. Eli Lilly ( LLY ) has added more than $250 billion over the same stretch, a gain topped only by Apple ( AAPL ) among the market's biggest stocks.

That's a 25% gain for the maker of Zepbound and Mounjaro against a 32% drop for the AI chip king through Friday's close. The gap kept widening Monday, a day before Nvidia's first earnings report since Jensen Huang's exit .

And it's not just one matchup. The AI trade has been bleeding from every direction since Nvidia peaked, with Alphabet ( GOOGL ) shedding about $640 billion in market value, SpaceX ( SPCX ) about $450 billion, and Micron ( MU ) about $300 billion, by Yahoo Finance calculations. Apple, Lilly, and Walmart ( WMT ) have been collecting.

It's the same lineup that showed up in October, when AI stocks lost about $5 trillion in less than a month and Lilly topped the winners' list.

Early in this bull market, the weight-loss drugmakers were Wall Street's other obsession. In the 15 months after the October 2022 low, Lilly and Novo Nordisk ( NVO ) gained about 92% on average, within shouting distance of the Magnificent Seven's 101%.

Then it fell apart. Novo lost about three-quarters of its value from its June 2024 peak, and the GLP-1 trade spent two years watching Big Tech run off with the bull market.

Now the roles have reversed. Lilly just pulled ahead of Nvidia over the past five years. The price tags have flipped too, with Lilly at roughly 27 times forward earnings, about two and a half times Nvidia's multiple, according to Yahoo Finance data.

The two worlds collided last week. In a video pitching Anthropic's IPO, CEO Dario Amodei said, "Cancer, Alzheimer's, heart disease, mental illness — these will be relics of the past in, I think, less than a decade."

Lilly CEO Dave Ricks wasn't buying it. "I think that would be amazing and I think it's not likely," he wrote on X , adding that "progress will likely be steady and incremental."

That doesn't necessarily make the weight-loss trade the one to chase now. Lilly stock sits about 30% above its 200-day moving average , the average of its last 200 closing prices.

Running that hot is nothing new for Lilly in this bull market. It's happened about one in seven trading days, nearly three times as often as in the years before. In 2023 and early 2024, even hotter streaks ended in dips of 7% to 12%. The last two ended in drops of more than 20%.

articles.title: AMD finalizes $8.2 billion World Labs acquisition, adds 'godmother of AI' as EVP and chief scientist

articles.body:
AMD ( AMD ) completed its $8.2 billion acquisition of Fei-Fei Li's World Labs on Monday, giving the company access to World Labs' AI models and research.

Li will also serve as executive vice president and chief scientist at the chip giant . Considered the 'godmother of AI,' Li's research is foundational to the AI boom.

World Labs develops AI models that simulate 3D environments to train robots to maneuver in both virtual and real worlds.

"Delivering the infrastructure that will power the next era of super intelligence requires us to optimize compute platforms and models together," AMD CEO Lisa Su said in a statement.

"We are thrilled to welcome Fei-Fei Li and the exceptional World Labs team to AMD. Their pioneering model research will help shape our future hardware, software, and systems. Together, we will enable researchers and developers across the ecosystem to push the boundaries of what AI can do," she added.

Yahoo Finance named Su its CEO of the Year for 2026 during its Invest conference last week.

The acquisition will help AMD better compete in the race to develop AI models that can power robots, a space that rival Nvidia ( NVDA ) has grabbed a strong foothold in thanks to its collection of open-weights models.

articles.title: Silicon Valley insiders urge Nvidia to restore Jensen Huang’s CEO role
articles.summary: Nvidia faces a potential 30 percent value loss in value without Jensen Huang, market analysts say, amid a stock downturn.
articles.body:
Tesla and SpaceX CEO Elon Musk and other Silicon Valley insiders are calling on chipmaker Nvidia to reinstate Jensen Huang, who resigned last week from the company he cofounded.

Musk is one of the 177,000 signatories to a petition titled “Stand With Jensen”, calling for the reinstatement of the executive, who resigned following reports of extramarital affairs, including one with an alleged Chinese spy.

“We are current and former NVIDIA employees, partners, shareholders, and supporters. We write with gratitude for Jensen Huang and with a clear demand to the Board: bring Jensen back while an independent investigation establishes the facts, unless and until you can provide compelling evidence that his removal is in NVIDIA’s best interests,” the letter published on the petition’s website said.

More privately, a group of Silicon Valley insiders is pushing to get Huang back in the role, with the Financial Times reporting that Huang is considering a comeback. The paper reported that an unnamed group of Silicon Valley insiders has put together a so-called war room and is lobbying the White House for support which is a move that may have been successful.

“A lot of people are asking Jensen, they think Jensen should go back. That certainly isn’t a bad idea,” United States President Donald Trump told reporters on Monday.

Much of Nvidia’s value is tied to Huang, with analysts estimating that the company could lose as much as 25 to 30 percent of its value without him .

Nvidia’s stock was trending downward in early trading on Wall Street, with US markets opening down 2.3 percent on the day. Over the last five days, the stock has dropped 8.5 percent and is down more than 25.7 percent over the last month.

The developments come as the White House moves to designate Nvidia, along with more than two dozen other companies, as “national champions” in the artificial intelligence industry, a new initiative intended to help the company secure more business overseas, according to reporting by The Wall Street Journal.

They also come as the Trump administration issued a rule on Monday that it would restrict China’s access to chips made by companies including Nvidia, as Trump begins a trip to China where he will meet with President Xi Jinping.

The restrictions are aimed at preventing Chinese companies from “circumventing” existing limits by using data centres in Southeast Asian countries such as Malaysia and Thailand to train their AI models.

“The rule is designed to ensure that existing restrictions on access to sensitive American technology cannot be circumvented through remote computing arrangements involving data centres in third countries,” the Department of Commerce said in a statement.

The new rule comes as the Commerce Department is scrambling to demonstrate that it is cracking down on Chinese access to sensitive US technology, following reports that the agency under Secretary Howard Lutnick turned a blind eye to the smuggling of advanced Nvidia AI chips into China.

articles.title: New retirement contribution limits give savers a modest boost next year
articles.summary: The amount of money you can set aside for retirement in tax-advantaged accounts is increasing next year, the IRS announced.
articles.body:
The amount of money you can set aside for retirement in tax-advantaged accounts is increasing next year, the IRS announced.

For 2027, the contribution limits for 401(k), 403(b), 457 plans, and the federal government's Thrift Savings Plan will increase to $25,500, up from $24,500 this year.

There's an $8,500 catch-up if you're 50 or older, up from $8,000. Folks who are 60 to 63 can contribute an additional $11,750 in 2027 in lieu of the $8,500, if your plan allows.

One reminder: Next year, if you are 50 or older and earned more than $155,000 in 2026, you must make your catch-up contributions on an after-tax basis in a Roth option in your employer-sponsored retirement plans

If your employer's plan doesn't offer a Roth 401(k) account, you might opt to contribute your catch-up amount to a Roth individual retirement account (IRA) if your income is below the IRS income threshold. Roth contributions are made with already-taxed dollars.

The IRA contribution limit will be $7,500 in 2027, unchanged from 2026, while the catch‑up contribution limit for people 50 and older bumps up to $1,100.

The limits apply to both traditional and Roth IRAs, though Roth IRA eligibility depends on your income. For Roth IRAs, the income limit range for contributing will increase slightly to between $158,000 and $173,000 for singles and heads of household. For married couples filing jointly, the range increases to between $250,000 and $260,000.

Balancing retirement saving with today's expenses

Most workers don't save the maximum permitted by the IRS, according to a Vanguard analysis of 5 million accounts. Last year, only 14% of savers ponied up the maximum contribution amount permitted by the IRS.

Participants who contributed the maximum tended to have higher incomes, were older, had longer tenures with their current employer, and had accumulated substantially higher account balances, according to David Stinnett, head of strategic retirement consulting at Vanguard.

In addition, more 401(k) participants are tapping their retirement savings years before they exit the workplace — a sign of how immediate needs often trump long-term saving.

The share of participants taking a hardship withdrawal rose to 3.4% last year, another study found — the third straight annual increase and more than double the 1.5% recorded in 2022.

Loans jumped as well — 22.2% had an outstanding loan, up from 12.4% the previous year.

"It's easy to say workers are raiding their retirement savings, but that misses what's really happening," Will Hansen, the Plan Sponsor Council of America's executive director, told Yahoo Finance.

articles.title: Kindness 'compounds': Warren Buffett donates $5.5 billion to family foundations
articles.summary: The billionaire stepped up his annual holiday donation.
articles.body:
Billionaire Warren Buffett announced on Monday that he will give 9.225 million Class B Berkshire Hathaway ( BRK-B ) shares — or roughly $5.5 billion — to four philanthropic foundations this Thanksgiving.

In his annual Thanksgiving letter, Buffett said he will give 3.69 million shares to the Susan Thompson Buffett Foundation, named after his late wife. He will split 1.845 million shares between his three children's philanthropic ventures: the Sherwood Foundation, the Howard G. Buffett Foundation, and NoVo Foundation.

"My children have given thoughtfully to worthy causes for decades, and I trust 100% both their abilities and their fidelity," the 96-year-old wrote.

This year's donation is more than four times greater than the amount set aside for charity last year. In July, the "Oracle from Omaha" promised to donate more than 99% of his entire Berkshire Hathaway fortune — more than $160 billion — to good causes by 2034 through these foundations.

"Last Thanksgiving I wrote that kindness is costless but also priceless," Buffett wrote in his letter on Monday. "A year later, I would only add that it compounds, and at a better rate than anything Charlie and I ever bought."

In September, Buffett stepped down as chair of Berkshire Hathaway, marking the end of his 50-plus-year tenure. He remains on the board of directors.

In his Thanksgiving letter, he encouraged others to give this holiday season.

"Much of my good fortune has come in the form of people who were kind to me and expected nothing in return. I'm grateful to every one of them," Buffett wrote. "This Thanksgiving, thank one of those selfless people in your own life. Better yet, be a benefactor for someone else."

articles.body:
Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick is facing pressure due to his approach to AI chip export controls as a national security scandal swirls around the tech company Nvidia, including from another member of President Trump’s Cabinet, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent.

Last week, reporting came out that Lutnick had a softer position on Nvida’s AI chip sales to China and did not place the Singaporean firm Megaspeed on the trade entity blacklist. Per Axios, Bessent confronted the Commerce secretary earlier this month over the failure to put Megaspeed on the Commerce Department’s entity list, which features companies that pose national security risks.

Megaspeed is central to the recent Nvidia scandal, which resulted in the company’s founder, Jensen Huang, resigning last week.

The reported confrontation between Bessent and Lutnick wouldn’t be the first time the two Trump administration officials have had tension. Here’s what you need to know about their rocky relationship:

Bessent previously called the Commerce secretary “an idiot” to his face over a minerals deal with Ukraine, according to the book “Regime Change: Inside the Imperial Presidency of Donald Trump” from New York Times journalists Maggie Haberman and Jonathan Swan.

Part of Haberman and Swan’s book focused on a conflict between Lutnick and Bessent over the minerals deal. Bessent, according to the Times journalists, was accused by Lutnick of having “screwed up” the deal. The Treasury secretary called a proposal from Lutnick “a s—-y deal” and told the Commerce secretary he was “an idiot.”

Bessent and Lutnick also battled it out for the Treasury secretary role before the beginning of the second Trump administration, Politico reported in late 2024 .

Last Friday, Bessent publicly stated that his department and other Trump administration officials had supported placing Megaspeed on the entity list.

“Treasury, War, USTR [U.S. Trade Representative] and State … were in favor of putting Megaspeed on the entity list for months,” Bessent said on CNBC’s “Squawk Box.”

“But Commerce has the pen. Commerce BIS [Bureau of Industry and Security] has the pen, and you will have to ask them about their internal processes,” he added.

Bessent also said in his CNBC appearance that he and Deputy Treasury Secretary Francis Brooke had “been pushing” Lutnick’s department to have Megaspeed on the entity list “for months.”

articles.title: TVS family feud deepens as Lakshmi asks dad Venu Srinivasan for partition of assets

articles.body: CHENNAI: Lakshmi Venu, daughter of Venu Srinivasan (VS), has formally sought partition of the joint family assets of the Venu Srinivasan branch of the larger TVS family, escalating a dispute over the division of family wealth. Her mother, Mallika Srinivasan, has backed her demand and called for an amicable settlement.A statement issued on Lakshmi’s behalf said she had, in a partition notice to her father, called upon him, as head of the family, to facilitate what she describes as a fair and lawful division of assets. Mallika said efforts to resolve the matter amicably had failed to make meaningful and timely progress. Venu Srinivasan’s side is yet to respond to this development.The rift in the Venu Srinivasan family centres on the division of family wealth and business interests. Wife Mallika Srinivasan and daughter Lakshmi argue that a March 2024 MoU did not settle the economic interests through a formal valuation and mutually agreed division. VS maintains that the split was fair, with Lakshmi taking over Sundaram-Clayton and son Sudarshan Venu taking over the TVS Motor business. The dispute escalated after a boardroom confrontation at Sundaram-Clayton earlier this year and recently took a legal turn, with family members filing caveats in Chennai courts. While VS maintains that ownership and control have been divided, Mallika and Lakshmi say the division of family wealth remains unresolved.Lakshmi’s claim is based on her interpretation of the Hindu Succession Act, 1956, as amended in 2005. She claimed that she is entitled to her rightful share in the joint family property and has an independent right to seek its partition. It is also founded on the equal rights of daughters recognised under section 6 of the Act.The assets covered by her claim include interests held through the VS Trust and other holding entities, encompassing businesses and assets allocated to the Venu Srinivasan branch under the 2020 TVS family arrangement. These include interests in TVS Holdings, TVS Motor Company, TVS Credit Services and Sundaram-Clayton.Lakshmi contends that the 2020 arrangement involving the wider TVS family did not partition assets within her immediate family. She has also argued that the March 2024 memorandum of understanding, which covered brand usage, trademarks and non-compete obligations, did not constitute an economic settlement involving the valuation and division of family wealth.She alleges that the concentration of beneficial interests in favour of her brother, Sudarshan Venu, has excluded her from her lawful entitlements. She views this as not only a breach of the law but also a breach of trust, maintaining that daughters’ rights to joint family property cannot be overridden through unilateral decisions or corporate arrangements.Supporting her daughter’s claim, Mallika said: “As a mother, to me, a son and daughter are equal in every respect. I do believe that Lakshmi has a legitimate share of the family assets, not unequal to that of Sudarshan.”Mallika reiterated her preference for a negotiated resolution through transparent dialogue, with equity, clarity and amity. She expressed hope that the family could move forward with grace and dignity.Money habits form by age 7. Is your child learning the right ones? Join the TOI Money Masterclass.
